beta.source: Weekly regression of the share's own returns on the FTSE ADX General Index (FADGI), the published index of the exchange the share is listed on — the market series is resolved from that listing rather than chosen by this study, and it is taken as of 2026-07-24. 159 weekly observations measured Friday close to Friday close on the exchange's own trading week, from 2023-06-16 to 2026-07-17, with both series screened for data quality before they are paired. The slope is a lead-lag sum — one lag, the contemporaneous return and one lead, added together. R-squared 0.1814, standard error 0.3147

beta_se.source: Standard error of the same regression

beta_blume.source: Blume cross-check reported with the same regression — two-thirds of the measured slope plus one-third of 1.0, the standard adjustment for the tendency of a measured beta to drift toward the market over time. beta_composite.source: The share's own returns regressed against an equal-weight composite of the exchange's own listed names instead of the published index — a basket assembled for this study alone, published for comparison and never adopted, because a hand-built basket is not the market this share is listed against. rf_terminal.source: Terminal risk-free rate, DERIVED from the house macro path [R-MACRO-01] as the terminal inflation of 2.00% plus the long-run real rate, NEVER quoted — a terminal rate somebody types is the single most terminal-value-sensitive number in a model. Under the peg the dirham real rate IS the dollar real rate, and the house convention builds it from the Federal Open Market Committee's own longer-run median policy projection plus the ten-year term premium less long-run United States inflation. This study had typed 3.25% on a 1.25% real assumption of its own; the derived figure is higher, so conforming LOWERS this study's value, which is the direction that shows the rule is not being fitted to a price

SETTLED ON EVIDENCE OUTSIDE THE PAGE, 7 September 2026, AND THE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY IN THIS DIRECTORY. The first-quarter 2026 earnings call transcript this study holds describes THAT SAME CONTRACT MATRIX in management's own words: "We are at a genuine inflection point for our gas carrier fleet. Starting this month, May 2026, 5 Das LNG carriers are progressively commencing long-term contracts with ADNOC Gas, 4 on 15-year contracts and 1 on a 7-year contract ... These are vessels that until now have been earning at spot rates." The dates on that matrix are contract COMMENCEMENTS, and the alternative requires the company to be presenting a fleet-wide contraction of contracted vessel-years as an inflection point upward on the slide it is describing. THE ADOPTED SIDE IS THE EVIDENCED ONE AND THE ANSWER DOES NOT MOVE — it was already the adopted side. The alternative is RETAINED here rather than deleted, for two reasons: it remains a legitimate downside framing of a path the company has not disclosed vessel by vessel, and dropping a judgement from this list would shrink the population the sign test [R-ENF-05] is computed over, which is not a thing to do to a test of one's own leaning.

The two differ because a published index is weighted by size and is dominated by the same large-capitalisation group this company belongs to, while an equal-weight composite gives the exchange's smallest names the same say as its largest. The alternative is published rather than buried because a difference of this size is a fact about index construction that a reader is entitled to see.

forecast_anchor.note:
THE FORECAST OPENS 38.90 PER CENT AGAINST A REVIEWED HALF THAT PRINTED 40.22, WHICH IS 3.3 PER CENT BELOW IT IN RELATIVE TERMS AND INSIDE THE MATERIALITY LINE. The delivered edition of this study anchored on the audited FY2025 year at 29.28 per cent and forecast 41.69 for 2026 — a rate that turned out to be very nearly right, because THE MARGIN WAS NOT WHAT THAT EDITION GOT WRONG. What it got wrong was SCALE: it forecast USD 5,003,932 thousand of 2026 revenue and the company earned USD 3,666,674 thousand in the first six months alone.

THE PATH FALLS FROM 38.90 PER CENT IN 2026 TO 31.92 IN 2030 AND THAT IS THE CLAIM TO INTERROGATE. It is not a margin assumption. Every rate in it is the company's own published time-charter equivalent — reported for the first and second quarters of 2026, disclosed for the third to 11 August on the share of vessel days it covers, and reverting from there to the average of the company's own 2024 and 2025 outcomes by 2030. The cost side is a fixed base escalated on the house inflation ladder plus a variable component per unit of the fleet's charter-equivalent revenue, both solved from the audited 2025 year and the reviewed 2026 half, with the reviewed 2025 half HELD OUT and reproduced to within 10.7 per cent. The margin is what those two lines leave.

THE ELEVEN VESSELS ANNOUNCED ON 7 AUGUST 2026, six of them very large crude carriers, enter at USD 1,300,000 thousand of committed and funded cost and earn from the third quarter. The reversion path is the CONSERVATIVE of the two the study publishes; the sustained path is shown beside it and is worth more, not less.

hybrid.note: THE TWO HALVES OF ONE TREATMENT. The perpetual capital securities rank ahead of the ordinary shares, so they are deducted here; a claim deducted from enterprise value must also be WEIGHTED in the cost of capital at its own cost, or the model subtracts a cheap tranche of capital without letting it price the value. The present value of the perpetual coupon is published beside the carrying value as the alternative deduction, because which of the two a reader prefers is a judgement and the study does not hide it inside one number.

range_basis.driver: the regression beta, across its own 90 per cent confidence interval, with the day-rate anchor and capital expenditure moving with it
range_basis.evidence: the own-stock regression against the published index of this company's own exchange gives a beta of 1.1032 with a standard error of 0.3147 over 159 weekly observations, so its 90 per cent interval runs 0.5855 to 1.6210. THE RANGE IS THE INTERVAL THE ESTIMATE ITSELF SUPPORTS rather than a judgement about how wrong it might be, and the corners take the HIGH beta for the bear and the LOW for the bull because a higher beta is a lower value. The day-rate anchor and capital expenditure move with each corner rather than being held, because a cost of capital at the top of its own interval describes a world in which charter rates are also weaker. The macro path does not move: terminal growth and the terminal risk-free rate both contain the same terminal inflation, so flexing them would make the bull corner inflation high and low at once.
